product.title: Mica istorie a religiei
product.description: Scrisă pentru credincioși, dar și pentru atei – și mai ales pentru tinerii cititori – Mică istorie a religiei ne poartă de-a lungul epocilor, de la primele manifestări de credință până în prezent. Fiind un ghid empatic, dar manifestând discernământ în ceea ce privește importanța credinței, Richard Holloway ne introduce în istoria și sistemele de credinţe ale religiilor majore ale omenirii: iudaismul, islamul, creștinismul, budismul și hinduismul. Holloway explorează și explică și proveniența credințelor religioase, modul cum diferențele de credință conduc uneori la ostilitate și violență, ce este o sectă și ce este un cult și nu numai. Pe tot parcursul cărții, autorul încurajează curiozitatea și toleranța, accentuează nuanța și misterul și reface cu calm sentimentul valorii credinței.   O carte bine scrisă, după a cărei lectură mulți dintre noi vor rămâne cu mai multe informații despre religie decât știau înainte... Times   Povestea lui Holloway abundă în fapte surprinzătoare. Financial Times

# A Small History of Religion: Exploring Belief Systems Across Ages

Unlock a deeper understanding of humanity's spiritual journey with *A Small History of Religion*. This essential non-fiction guide is designed for everyoneâwhether you are a committed believer, an inquisitive atheist, or simply a young reader curious about the worldâs faiths.

Authored by Richard Holloway, this acclaimed book takes readers on a sweeping historical voyage. It guides us through the origins and evolution of belief systems, examining everything from humanity's earliest manifestations of faith right up to the present day. Understanding global religions has never been more crucial, and Holloway offers an insightful, comprehensive overview that is both intellectually rigorous and deeply compassionate.

## Navigating the Worldâs Major Faiths

Whether you are new to comparative religion or looking to refresh your knowledge, *A Small History of Religion* provides detailed explorations into the core tenets and histories of the world's major traditions. The book systematically covers:

*   **Judaism:** Tracing its ancient roots and enduring cultural impact.
*   **Christianity:** Exploring its historical development and global reach.
*   **Islam:** Understanding its theological foundations and spread across continents.
*   **Buddhism:** Delving into the philosophy and practices of this profound spiritual tradition.
*   **Hinduism:** Examining one of the world's oldest and most complex belief systems.

Holloway doesn't just list doctrines; he explores the *provenance* of these beliefs. The text thoughtfully addresses how differences in faith can sometimes lead to conflict, offering crucial definitions for topics like cults versus sects. Throughout its pages, the author consistently encourages curiosity, tolerance, and an appreciation for the mystery inherent in belief itself.

### Why This Book is Essential Reading

More than just a history lesson, this book serves as a powerful meditation on empathy and understanding. Richard Hollowayâs narrative style manages to be both deeply scholarly and refreshingly accessible. As noted by *Financial Times*, the story is filled with surprising facts that challenge assumptions and deepen perspectives. The ultimate goal of the writing is not merely to inform, but to foster a sense of shared humanityâa call to embrace nuance and curiosity regarding belief.

Discover why this book has been praised for providing readers with significantly more knowledge about religion than they thought possible.

***

### Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**Is this book only for religious people?**
No. While it discusses major religions, the content is explicitly written for believers, non-believers, and young readers alike, focusing on understanding human spirituality in general terms.

**What makes this guide unique?**
It goes beyond simple historical timelines by exploring the *empathetic* side of belief, examining how faith influences culture and conflict while promoting tolerance.
